A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoGramBench and the same Program-to-Geometry research. Their main texts, figures, tables, mathematical content, and complete appendices support comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 17 LLMs, benchmark comparisons, a drawing-language experiment, and analyses of model responses.

after.justification: v2 reports evaluations of 19 LLMs, subtype results, supervised fine-tuning and token-budget experiments, and prediction-variability analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed task, three-level taxonomy, text-plus-code input, answer format, and benchmark construction approach remain unchanged. The added fine-tuning and budget-forcing studies apply existing s1 procedures as diagnostic experiments; no new solver or model architecture is proposed.

E1.justification: Appendix D newly uses s1k general-reasoning examples for training alongside GeoGramBench examples. Evaluation retains the same 500-problem benchmark and AIME24/MATH-500 coverage. The six subtypes classify existing problems; real-world 3D scenarios remain future work.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GPT-5, Qwen3-235B-Thinking-2507, and Qwen3-32B, while removing LIMO-32B, changing the total from 17 to 19 models. Figure 1 additionally includes R1-Distillation-32B in its benchmark comparisons. The shortened DeepSeek distillation names represent retained comparators.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce a 300-training/200-test split, training additions of 50–300 GeoGramBench examples, and budget-forcing settings with N-Ignore values 0, 1, 2, 4, and 6. v2 also adds subtype-stratified evaluation and regroups MATH-500 reasoning levels in Figure 2. The main zero-shot protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D and E add controlled tests of domain-data scarcity and whether longer reasoning improves performance. Table 1 adds subtype diagnostics, and Figure 2 adds evaluation by geometric complexity. The drawing-language experiment and detailed QwQ-32B case studies are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 already reports eight responses per question at temperature 0.6. Appendix F and Table 5 newly report descriptive standard deviations for selected models, overall and by difficulty. This adds uncertainty reporting without documenting increased sampling, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive subtype and ablation results; GPT-5 reports 75.01% overall accuracy, and Qwen3-235B-Thinking-2507 reaches 49.05% on Abstract. Retained entries also change: GPT-o1 Abstract accuracy changes from 43.35% to 44.67%, and QwQ-32B overall accuracy from 67.20% to 67.12%. These are reported revisions under the same stated main protocol, without an explanation of rerunning or recomputation.

T1.justification: No substantive formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced or revised. The internal-representation hypothesis moves from Section 7 to Appendix H with its conceptual content preserved. New subtype labels and descriptive statistics do not constitute new theory.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the Program-to-Geometry task, a curated 500-problem benchmark with three complexity levels, and persistent difficulties with abstract geometry, with every evaluated model below 50% on Abstract. Additional models and behavioral evidence support these retained central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for subtype difficulty, identifies common failure patterns, and interprets data-scaling and budget-forcing plateaus as spatial-representation limitations. Appendix I explicitly discusses missing real-world 3D coverage, qualitative error analysis, uncertain CoT faithfulness, and unestablished transfer benefits. The original representation hypothesis is retained in Appendix H.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly documents Asymptote syntax validation, renderability checks, and diagram adjustments. Appendices D–E specify DeepSeek-R1 reasoning distillation and the Wait-token intervention. A new reproducibility statement says evaluation code and execution instructions accompany the supplementary materials. These disclosures do not establish changes to previously conducted curation.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a targeted discussion of symbolic graphics, covering SGP-Bench, SVG Taxonomy, SVGenius, SGP-GenBench, and Chat2SVG, and distinguishes geometry reasoning from SVG perception and generation. References for newer models are added and LIMO is removed; the central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted rewrites to the taxonomy rationale, results narrative, conclusion, and limitations, and adds a task-data-format explanation. The hypothesis moves to Appendix H and the taxonomy prompt to C.7. Much of the introduction, task definition, curation description, and case-study text remains closely preserved.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a much denser matrix of level averages and subtype scores. Figures 1–2 are redesigned, Figure 5 adds a subtype-distribution visualization, and Tables 2–5 provide new displays. Figures are relocated and the document adopts conference formatting. The expanded main table is substantially harder to read at normal page size.

improvement.justification: Controlled data and token-budget experiments test explanations that v1 mainly inferred from scores and response traces; subtype diagnostics and clearer limitations also improve the paper. These benefits are tempered by unexplained revisions to retained scores and aggregation inconsistencies in Tables 4–5. Table 5 additionally repeats GPT-o1-preview with different values. The new evidence is useful, but reporting problems limit the overall gain.
